raw_text: Follow `@.agents/memories/20-tooling.md` and built-in functions. `.rulesync/` is the source of truth: author changes there first in `rules`, `skills`, `subagents`, `commands`, `hooks`, and `mcp`. Generated target directories and prompt files are build artifacts. Regenerate them from RuleSync instead of editing them by hand. Keep shared root `AGENTS.md` content in the overview rule; keep follow-up split rules off AGENTS-writing targets. Fix incorrect generated output in `.rulesync/` and re-run `rulesync`. Keep frontmatter RuleSync-compliant; add target-specific blocks only for real runtime differences. Keep commands deterministic and hooks advisory and portable. Route hook-only targets through generated rules or hook text, not unavailable skill or command surfaces. Use `rulesync generate --check` as the consistency gate, then `rulesync generate` for intentional changes. Review source and generated diffs together; do not hand-edit generated target directories to patch a platform quirk. **Verify target configurations** using `.rulesync/verification/` checklists before committing. Use RuleSync commands directly instead of manually reproducing catalog, prompt, incident, or graph logic from source. Resolve `Multiple root rulesync rules found` by ensuring only one root overview rule exists. Tab cycles **primary** agents only; `<REDACTED_USER>` invokes subagents. `dotnet-architect` is a primary OpenCode agent. Targets include GitHub Copilot CLI; target support is asymmetric. Also supports Gemini CLI and Factory Droid via generated .NET routing/advisories/hooks.
